items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: He was really Carnage in the band then on Trinidad... I never had a chance to play with the original Excelsior.

ctx.x: He used to use the Holy Ghost's bar, I play when I was playing. Sure. He'd play a solo trumpet. No, I didn't know. And he, that was a powerful man.

In other words, he kept all the music and everything. He was a good reader. Strictly most of the reader. He had the Eureka. Yeah, he enjoyed that Eureka then. He was really Carnage in the band then on Trinidad. No, Willie had died. He was out of there then. He was out of there. But I'm more sure that Landry had played with Carnage. He had been a member of the Eureka. Yeah, yeah, yeah. For a long time. He and Rodgers both. He and Ernest Rodgers both. He's been members of Eureka for years. I never had a chance to…
Did that Ormond come through? That's the move.

items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: And it'd take like Buddy Petit and Chris Crom, they'd be playing at them out on the lakefront... Well, I played several of those songs before they broke those camps down. I had a chance to play plenty of those.

ctx.x: That's good. He told us that and I never even thought of that there'd be anybody that we'd ever meet, you know. And all of a sudden he tells us that it's nice to have him. That's Earl Foster. Did you ever see any other pictures of Buddy Petit?
Well, no, of course I saw Buddy himself.
Yeah, I've seen you ever heard about pictures of Buddy Petit. I've never even saw Buddy at once. I've seen some more pictures of Buddy.
